If it keeps asking for mail account password then it sounds like your passwords are not being saved.

When you enter the requested password, did you select the checkbox to remember password before clicking on OK?

  • Is anything displaying in this area?

Ok, this may not answer all of your questions, but it's a start: - The 'beauty' of variable width is that no font specification is sent, allowing recipient full control of that. That is why I encourage setting both Latin and OtherWritingSystems to be identical and I set my font size on every option, including plain text. re :Regarding an earlier suggestion, I logged into Thunderbird using the password, went to the Settings page to check passwords, and I had to log into Thunderbird, again to check to see what password is listed.

I'm presuming the passwords were saved. But...you said you had to log into Thunderbird again to check to see password.

It's normal to need to logon to see saved passwords, but the password to logon to mail accounts is not the same password you use to get access to saved passwords ...unless you are not talking about mail account passwords.

I'm now wondering if you are not talking about logging on to mail accounts - I'm wondering if you are being asked for a 'Primary Password'.

Have you set up Thunderbird to use 'Primary Password' ? It would be shown here:

  • Settings > Privacy & Security
  • Scroll down to 'Passwords' section.
  • Is this checkbox selected : 'Use a Primary Password' ?

if yes then you will be asked to logon using the 'primary password' at the start of each session and also you would be asked to enter the 'primary password' when accessing saved passwords.

Is there a reason why you have set up to use a 'Primary Password' - which should be a unique password not a mail account password or a User Account password. Normally you would set up a Primary Password only if you share your computer and your User Account with other people and you want additional protection from prying eyes to stop them seeing your actual mail account passwords. See info Primary Passwords' https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/protect-your-thunderbird-passwords-primary-password

content:
Opa, a fim de conhecimento, vou relatar aqui como o processo foi resolvido por aqui.

O Thunderbird não reconheceu de jeito algum o certificado emitido pelo zimbra ssl/tls, o que tivemos que a dedo colocar pra ele ser reconhecido.

Vai na Aba "geral" nas configurações do Thunderbird, arrasta até o final e vai em "editor de configurações" Procura por "network.security.ports.banned.override" > Clica na bolinha de "texto" > adiciona "995" e clica no "v" Volta na aba "privacidade e segurança" > vai em gerenciar certificados > aba servidores > Adiciona exceção e dentro da caixa que abriu, coloca > mail.provedor.com.br:995 Clica em confirmar exceção e verifica se apareceu lá dentro o mail.provedor.com.br:995 Volta na aba geral do Thunderbird > editor de configurações > procura novamente por "network.security.ports.banned.override" > Clica na bolinha de "texto" > adiciona "465" e clica no "v" Volta na aba "privacidade e segurança" > vai em gerenciar certificados > aba servidores > Adiciona exceção e dentro da caixa que abriu, coloca > mail.provedor.com.br:465 Clica em confirmar exceção e verifica se apareceu lá dentro o mail.provedor.com.br:465 Vai na Aba "geral" nas configurações do Thunderbird, arrasta até o final e vai em "editor de configurações" Procura por "security.tls.version.min" > altera pro valor 1 Procura por "security.tls.version.enable-deprecated" > altera para true Clica "ctrl + shift + q" pra fechar o Thunderbird Abre novamente e adiciona a conta, agora selecionando o certificado ssl/tls nas portas padrões tanto pop3 quanto smtp

Espero que seja útil pra comunidade. Abraços!
